summary: Midday throughput collapse in dedicated pool caused by repeated short hot-loop streams from a single tenant
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 11:24 UTC, AtlasAI observed a sharp reduction in throughput and increase in p95/p99 latency on their dedicated capacity pool (us-east). The drop coincided with a cluster-wide spike in short-lived streaming requests from a single tenant namespace. Impact: customer-facing endpoints saw request timeouts and elevated error rates, blocking AtlasAI's inference pipelines during a peak window. Environment: dedicated pool (dp-az-us-east-1a), production, AtlasAI reserved capacity. Observed behavior: p50 unaffected, p95/p99 increased from 200ms to 3.5s; throughput (rps) dropped ~45% for the pool. Root symptoms resembled noisy-tenant small-stream fanout, autoscaler misprediction, and transient GPU slot shortages.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In a dedicated pool with multiple tenants, issue many parallel short streaming infer requests (100-300ms each) from a single tenant across many lightweight connections.
2) Ensure requests use medium-length context (256-512 tokens) and frequent reconnects (keep-alive not reused).
3) Observe scheduler queue growth and autoscaler failing to scale fast enough, leading to slot fragmentation and blocked batches.
4) Monitor GPU allocation logs and kernel queue depth to confirm slot exhaustion and kernel stalls.

investigation_notes: 11:35 UTC - Support confirmed customer symptom and collected tenant request traces and X-Request-Id headers.
11:42 UTC - SRE observed pattern: high frequency of extremely short streams (~50-300ms) from a single tenant producing many small batches that serialized on GPU-side batcher.
11:55 UTC - Autoscaler: predictive window missed the microburst; scale-up latency ~70s which was insufficient for the short-lived load, creating slot contention.
12:10 UTC - KV cache pinning not a factor; cache hit ratio stable. Primary bottleneck was slot allocation and small-batch serialization increasing kernel launch overhead.
12:22 UTC - Confirmed correlated increase in kernel-queue-depth and nvlink busy% across nodes in the pool.

Hypothesis: a noisy-tenant microburst pattern caused excessive slot fragmentation and forced the autoscaler to oscillate; background maintenance tasks (checkpoint-writer) amplified slot unavailability on some nodes.

resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation (2026-03-10 12:28 UTC): Applied a tenant-scoped soft throttle (RPS cap) to reduce microburst fanout and prevent slot serialization. This restored median+tail latencies and throughput stabilized within 10-15 minutes.
Autoscaler tuning (2026-03-10 13:40 UTC): Reduced prediction window and increased scale-up aggressiveness for dedicated pools during business hours to better handle microbursts.
Runtime change (deployed 2026-03-11): Merged PR #1357 to the serving runtime to batch short streams more effectively and lower kernel-launch overhead for sub-300ms streams.
Follow-up: SRE/Eng to run a controlled chaos test and add a policy to detect high short-stream fanout patterns automatically to trigger temporary throttles. Action tracked in INT-4021.
Customer communication: Informed AtlasAI of mitigations and changes; agreed on a staged rollout of runtime patch and detection rule. Customer accepted workaround and labeled as resolved.
Postmortem planned and scheduled in Confluence page.
